questions.q: Consider three boxes, each containing <math><mn>10</mn></math> balls labelled <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><mo>…</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><mn>10</mn></math>. Suppose one ball is randomly drawn from each of the boxes. Denote by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>, the label of the ball drawn from the <math><msup><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi></mrow></msup></math> box, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>. Then, the number of ways in which the balls can be chosen such that <math><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Each box contains 10 balls numbered from 1 to 10.

n1, n2, n3 are numbers on the balls drawn from the box B1, B2 and B3 respectively such that n1<n2<n3.

i.e., all 3 numbers n1, n2, n3 must be different and can be arranged only in one way (increasing).

Now n1, n2, n3 can be selected in 10C3 ways.

Hence, total number of ways =10C3.1=10C3=10!3!7!=10×9×83×2=120.

y=5  x=5→x=y=z=5

questions.q: All the letters of the word PUBLIC are written in all possible orders and these words are written as in a dictionary with serial numbers. Then the serial number of the word PUBLIC is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given word is PUBLIC

Arranging the letters alphabetically, we get

BCILPU

When the word starts with any of the letters B/C/I/L, the number of possibilities=5!×4=480

Now when the word starts with PB, then the number of possibilities=4!=24

Now when the word starts with PC, then the number of possibilities =4!=24

Now when the word starts with PI, then the number of possibilities =4!=24

Now when the word starts with PL, then the number of possibilities =4!=24

Now when the word starts with PUBC, then the number of possibilities=2!=2

Now when the word starts with PUBI, then the number of possibilities =2!=2

Now when the word starts with PUBLC, then the number of possibilities=1

Now when the word starts with PUBLIC, then the number of possibilities =1

Rank =480+24×4+2×2+1×2=582

Hence, rank of the work PUBLIC is 582.

questions.solution:
As we know that the product of numbers is even when at least one of the number must be even.

Hence total subsets of A in which product of numbers is even = Total subsets – total subsets in which all the elements are odd

=2100-250=250250-1.

questions.q: Number of ways of arranging <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn></math> identical books into <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math> identical shelves where any number of shelves may remain empty is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have 4 identical shelves in which any number of shelves can be empty.

So, we will put 3, 2, 1, 0 shelves empty one by one.

Also, the non-empty shelves won't require internal arrangement as all the shelves are identical.

3 Shelf empty: 8,0,0,0→1 way

2 shelf empty: (7,1,0,0)(6,2,0,0)(5,3,0,0)(4,4,0,0)→4 ways

1 shelf empty: (6,1,1,0)(3,3,2,0)(5,2,1,0)(4,2,2,0)(4,3,1,0)→5ways

0 shelf empty: (1,2,3,2)(5,1,1,1)(2,2,2,2)(3,3,1,1)(4,2,1,1)→5 ways

Total =15 ways

When ​​​​​​​i+j+k=15 then possible cases are

AHMST

Now when the word starts with TA, then the number of possibilities=3!=6

questions.q: The number of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn></math> digit numbers, that can be formed using all the digits of the number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>123412341</mn></math> so that the even digits occupy only even places, is ______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
According to the question,

1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4

there are four even digits as 2 and 4 are repeating two times each. 
So, the even digits will occupy the even places in 4!(2! 2!) = 6 ways

3 and 1 are repeating two and three times respectively.
So, the remaining places will be occupied by odd digits in 5!(3! 2!)=10 ways

Therefore, total 9 digits that can be formed = 6×10 = 60.
Hence, the answer is 60.

questions.q: The total number of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo></math>digit numbers whose sum of digits is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn></math>, is ..........
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let xyz be the three-digit number such that

x+y+z=10, x≥1, y≥0, z≥0

Let x-1=t⇒x=1+t

So, x≥1⇒t+1≥1⇒t≥0

Also, x+y+z=10⇒t+y+z=10-1=9

So, t+y+z=9, 0≤t, y, z≤9

Thus, total number of non-negative integral solution =C3-19+3-1=C211=11.102=55

But for t=9, x=10, so required number of integers =55-1=54.
